solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: French writer describing parking in grounds of university

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the writer's name encircles the next piece

parts.note: Albert Camus, the French novelist of The Outsider
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A French author writes about the car parks on a university site.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds and buildings of a college or university are known collectively by this Latin-derived term.

clue.text: Outline of paper cup

indicators.note: the letters come out of the run of words paper cup, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Someone sketches the shape of a paper cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief summary or quick insight, borrowed from French, is a kind of outline of a subject.

clue.text: Portion free with good English game bird

parts.note: a portion is a part
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A share of a game bird, given away along with good English cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump ground-dwelling bird shot for sport and food, so a game bird.

clue.text: Replace wonderful watch studded with diamonds

parts.note: super means wonderful

indicators.note: a thing studded with gems has them set into it, so the next piece is set inside the watch word

parts.note: to watch is to see
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone swaps out a superb diamond-encrusted wristwatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' looks like a noun, a timepiece, but it is the verb, giving SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the place of something older is to supplant it, a synonym of replace.

clue.text: Most ornate hotel in Swiss sports centre

indicators.note: ornate means elaborately worked, so these letters are rearranged into a fancier order

parts.note: the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel

explanation.surface: The fanciest hotel in a Swiss resort.
explanation.definitionFit: This Alpine town in Switzerland is a famous winter-sports resort that has twice hosted the Winter Olympics.

clue.text: Individual's runs, perhaps

definitions.meaning: read as 'individual is', the plural noun for one-person things or unattached people
in cricket a run taken one at a time is one of these

explanation.surface: A batsman's personal tally of runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Individual's' stands for 'is'. In cricket, a batsman who scores runs one at a time is taking these.
explanation.definitionFit: Single people or single things are individuals; and runs of one apiece are an example in cricket scoring.

clue.text: Opener for Middlesex departs, one having been caught by leg fielder

indicators.note: a thing caught is held between the other letters, so the numeral goes inside
the opener is the first letter of the county name

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
I is the Roman numeral one
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A Middlesex opening batsman is out, caught by a fielder on the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: Middlesex is an English county cricket team. 'by' joins the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielding position on the leg side, near the bowler, also names the player stationed there.

clue.text: Composer's party line

parts.note: a rave is a wild party

explanation.surface: A composer's attitude to parties, or his musical line.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Boléro.

clue.text: Go blue getting lower

parts.note: a go in a game is a turn
feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: Becoming sad as one's mood sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce volume, heat or a collar is to bring it lower, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Turtle quietly burrowing into ground

indicators.note: a creature burrowing into earth ends up inside it, so this letter goes within

parts.note: terrain is ground
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A turtle silently digging itself into the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater turtle of North America, often kept as a pet, so a kind of turtle.

clue.text: Various pelicans, say

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned word for sundry or several
pelicans plunge into water for fish, so they are birds that plunge

explanation.surface: A list of different pelicans, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means sundry; and pelicans, plunging after fish, are creatures that dive.

clue.text: Twenty by end of over — I record that

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cricket official noting twenty runs at the end of an over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces side by side. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who keeps the tally of runs could say of each one that they log it.

clue.text: Catch boy by yard pointing to woman with lodgers

parts.note: to land a fish is to catch it
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Catching a lad in the yard who points to the woman running a lodging house.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who lets rooms to tenants, often in her own house, is their landlord.

clue.text: For example, spaniel's tail

definitions.meaning: a spaniel is one example of a hound or canine pet
to tail someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A spaniel's wagging tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is an instance of a canine; and to tail is to follow persistently, a verb sense.

clue.text: Relish not working — that may bring reprimand

parts.note: a relish or sauce added to food is a dressing
a system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: A broken sauce dispenser that earns someone a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe scolding is an idiomatic name for a reprimand.

clue.text: Horrific experience of man losing a thousand on horse

indicators.note: losing something means dropping it, so the thousand comes away from the chess man

parts.note: a knight is a man in chess
K stands for a thousand, from kilo
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A gambler's ordeal after losing a grand on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the horse after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying ordeal or a very bad dream is a horrific experience.

clue.text: Doing wrong wearing the German pistol

indicators.note: the German word wears the other piece like clothing around it

parts.note: der is a German word for the
erring is doing wrong

explanation.surface: A German misbehaving with a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pocket pistol named after its American maker, Henry Deringer.

clue.text: Decisive gunfight? Record inaccurate

parts.note: to shoot a film is to record it
a guess that is out is wrong

explanation.surface: A disputed record of a showdown between gunmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun battle settling a dispute, as in Westerns, is a decisive exchange of fire.

clue.text: Dealer in Lancashire and Cheshire?

parts.note: seemingly a trader based in two English counties, but both are also names of cheeses he would sell

explanation.surface: A businessman operating in two north-west English counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire and Cheshire are English counties, but also crumbly English cheeses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who trades in cheese would deal in varieties such as these.

clue.text: Second flaming offence

parts.note: a fire that is in is still burning

explanation.surface: A second offence in a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A transgression against moral or religious law is an offence.

clue.text: Extra owed yet to arrive

parts.note: something over is left over or extra
money due is owed

explanation.surface: An extra debt that has not yet been paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something late, not having come when expected, is still awaited.

clue.text: Initially, carry on about too much material

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word carry

parts.note: OTT is over the top, too much
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone banging on endlessly about something.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft fabric woven from the fibres of a plant is a common material.

clue.text: I, alone, misled about the short opera

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece
misled means led astray, so these letters wander into a new order
short means cut off at the end, so drop the last letter of the word

parts.note: the article taken as a word

explanation.surface: Someone lonely and deceived about a brief opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misled' turns I ALONE into IOLANE, which goes 'about' TH, the word the made 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera about fairies and the House of Lords.

clue.text: Put the wind up a member crossing lake

indicators.note: the piece runs across the lake, so the lake letter sits within it

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone panics a member of a club by rowing across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put the wind up' is British slang for frighten.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten or startle someone, a verb sense synonymous with scare.

clue.text: Character devouring British steak

indicators.note: devouring means eating up, so the word takes the other letter inside

parts.note: the tone of a place is its character

explanation.surface: A personality type wolfing down a British steak.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef with a bone in the shape of a letter, a classic steak.

clue.text: Such a one may suit you

definitions.text: Such a one may suit you

parts.words: Such a one may suit you
parts.note: seems to mean a person who would be right for you, but means one who makes you a suit

explanation.surface: A matchmaker's line about a compatible partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothier who makes made-to-measure suits literally fits a client with one.

clue.text: Fruit old lady tried initially to tuck into as well

indicators.note: to tuck one thing into another is to put it inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: too means as well
an old lady, colloquially, is one's mother, ma

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of tried

explanation.surface: Mum too tried tucking into a piece of fruit at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically, this red salad item is a berry, so a fruit.

clue.text: Game flows

definitions.meaning: a board game, called checkers in America
currents of air through a room, or swallows of drink

explanation.definitionFit: A board game played with round pieces; and currents of cold air are flows through a room.

clue.text: Flight impressed head of Etihad

parts.note: a document impressed with a seal is stamped

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An airline boss pleased with a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Etihad is the Abu Dhabi airline, which makes 'Flight' look like an air journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden panicked rush of a herd is headlong flight.

clue.text: Racing trainer sacking one for straying off course

indicators.note: racing about, the letters run into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A racehorse trainer who gets fired for going off track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' takes the I (one) out of TRAINER before 'Racing' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering from the proper path, like a knight errant, is straying.
